$comment: Screen registry for the ui-mock-diff skill. `mock` is relative to mocks/, `route` is the React route on the running dev server. A screen with route:null is mock-only (not implemented yet) and is skipped by the impl/diff steps.

screens.name: overview
screens.note: New. Summary of the four inbound surfaces, quota, spend, failover.

screens.name: routing
screens.note: Preference chain for one surface/scenario/lane. Absorbs RouterPreferences + TierEditor + RouterUtilization.

screens.name: routing-passthrough
screens.note: The passthrough half — today's hardcoded behaviour for chat/completions and responses, made visible and reversible.

screens.name: routing-edit
screens.note: The chain after Edit. The screen reads until then: drag handles, row toggles, the row menu, Add target and the constraint controls only work in this state, and one Revert / Save in band 3 covers the chain and its constraints together, because one write carries both. While editing, the surface tabs, the mode switch and the profile picker are disabled: each would load another profile or hide the chain, and the unsaved edit would go with it. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click, so there is no route that lands on it.

screens.name: providers
screens.note: Subscriptions list. Providers gained two sub-entries because its 18rem rail already grouped them under these two headings, and that rail cost the detail pane 288px it needed — account emails truncated, six price columns collapsed to dashes. Quota is the column this list exists for: a subscription is the only provider kind that stops serving without anyone changing anything.

screens.name: providers-keys
screens.note: API keys list. Different columns from Subscriptions on purpose — a key has a secret and a price list where a subscription has accounts, a plan and a window that runs out, and the union would be four dashes per row on one side. 'not set' is a real row: a provider can exist with no key, and that is why its models never answer.

screens.name: provider-subscription
screens.note: One subscription provider: accounts, request shape, models. Full width now that the rail is gone — reached from the Subscriptions list, back via the breadcrumb, the same way a token detail works.

screens.name: provider-subscription-edit
screens.note: The subscription provider after Edit: tier overrides and the model and provider switches only work in this state, one Revert / Save covers them, and Refresh / Add subscription / Test all are locked until one is pressed. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click.

screens.name: provider-apikey-edit
screens.note: The api_key provider after Edit: tier and effort overrides, the switches and Replace only work in this state, Remove appears red beside Revert / Save, and the page actions and Test all are locked. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click.

screens.name: provider-apikey-remove
screens.note: Remove's confirmation. An irreversible action is a red button that goes through an AlertDialog stating what goes with it, never window.confirm. Mock-only because the state sits behind two clicks.

screens.name: provider-apikey
screens.note: One API-key provider — masked key, real prices, per-model apiStyle override. Full width for the same reason as provider-subscription.

screens.name: providers-connect
screens.note: Add-provider flow. Absorbs ConnectChoiceDialog + ProviderConnectFlow + ImportCredentialsDialog + ManualCallbackDialog. KNOWN DIFF ~15% dark: the mock draws step 2 of three, mid-authentication; the route opens on step 1. Capture limitation, not an implementation gap.

screens.name: providers-connect-device
screens.note: Codex signing in with a device code: Rialto shows a one-time code and auth.openai.com/codex/device, and continues once the code is entered. Codex has no browser sign-in here: its OAuth client only redirects to localhost:1455, which a remote or containerised install never receives. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click and a live upstream call. The code is a placeholder: its real format is only seen on a live sign-in.

screens.name: providers-connect-codex-failed
screens.note: Codex before a code has been asked for, with the last attempt's error still on record. The failure card sits straight under the choice grid here rather than under a waiting card, so it carries its own top gap — without one it touched the choices. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click and depends on an account that has already failed.

screens.name: providers-connect-models
screens.note: Step 3 of the add-provider flow (ConnectModelsStep), which the mock set stopped short of. Route is null because the step is a state of /providers/connect rather than its own path, so a capture would land on step 1.
screens.$comment: Reuses the provider detail model table on purpose: same decision, made before the provider takes traffic.

screens.name: access-tokens
screens.note: Per-client credentials for /v1/*. Top level rather than under Settings: Providers is outbound, this is the same question inbound, and a list carrying per-token spend, rotation and revocation is operations rather than configuration. Issuing happens in a dialog over this list — access-token-issue.html and access-token-issued.html are its two steps.

screens.name: access-token
screens.note: One token's own page: rotate, re-scope, revoke. Reached by clicking a row, which is where those actions used to live — as row actions they sat one mis-aimed click from every row of a table of live credentials. Route needs `bun run db:seed:demo`, whose token ids are deterministic; without it the capture lands on the not-found state.

screens.name: access-token-issue
screens.note: Step 1 of issuing: the form, in a dialog over the list. A dialog rather than an inline panel because naming a token is decided against the ones that already exist, and the inline form pushed that list off the page to ask. Route is null because it is a state of /access-tokens rather than a path of its own.

screens.name: access-token-issued
screens.note: Step 2 of issuing: the one-time reveal, in the same dialog. The panel swaps its contents rather than opening a second one — closing it is the last chance to copy the plaintext, so it happens where the operator is already looking. Route is null for the same reason as step 1.

screens.name: activity
screens.note: Sessions tab. Absorbs Sessions + Usage + ApiCost.

screens.name: activity-requests
screens.note: Per-request log with Requested → Sent, scenario and token attribution.

screens.name: activity-usage
screens.note: Usage tab. Subscription windows grouped by provider, each account's plan with its multiplier (Max 5x / Max 20x, Codex Pro 5x / Pro 20x), including the per-model weekly windows Overview drops; utilization over time; per-token spend. No export. Reads /api/usage, /api/usage/history and /api/subscriptions (provider grouping and rate_limit_tier). KNOWN DIFF: the mock draws two providers and five accounts; an install with fewer renders fewer rows, and the missing rows shift every section below them. Data, not design — the section order, heads and column layout line up.

screens.name: activity-session
screens.note: Session detail, Routing trace tab: newest first, paged. Route stays null because /activity/sessions/:sessionId needs a real captured session id, which differs per install — a hardcoded one would shoot the not-found state.

screens.name: activity-session-conversation
screens.note: Session detail, Conversation tab: the archived messages newest first, paged like the trace. Prose is shown; tool calls, tool results and injected context are one folded line each until opened. Route null for the same reason as activity-session.

screens.name: activity-logs
screens.note: Server log tail, newest first. Each line is one row and opens to the whole event. Absorbs LogViewer and its four sub-components. KNOWN DIFF: the mock shows one line opened; the implementation opens none until clicked.

screens.name: settings
screens.note: Server section. Absorbs SettingsPage.

screens.name: settings-access
screens.note: Admin access: Cloudflare Access, and the way back in when it breaks — a browser on the host, reached over an SSH port-forward. There is no bootstrap token (APIKEY is gone). The per-client /v1 tokens moved to their own top-level section. KNOWN DIFF: the mock depicts an install with Cloudflare Access configured (signed-in email, populated policy rows); an install without it correctly renders the other state, including the notice that remote admin access is closed, which the mock is never in a position to show.

screens.name: settings-access-edit
screens.note: Admin access after Edit. The team domain and AUD read until Edit is pressed — they are set once and left alone, and a stray keystroke in either shuts remote browsers out. The dry run (Verify) only exists while editing, one Revert / Save covers the pair, and Audit log is locked because leaving would drop the edit; Open Zero Trust stays live because the AUD is copied from there. Mock-only because the state sits behind a click.

screens.name: settings-access-turnoff
screens.note: Saving an emptied pair turns Access off, the one save the gate allows without a dry run, and it closes /api/* to every remote browser — possibly the one saving. So it asks first, in an AlertDialog that says who loses access. Mock-only because the state sits behind an edit and a click.

screens.name: settings-logging
screens.note: Log level, request/message capture, retention per store.

screens.name: settings-personas
screens.note: Absorbs Personas + PersonaView + PersonaEdit — three routes for one object.

screens.name: settings-statusline
screens.note: Absorbs StatusLineConfigDialog + its six sub-components. Modal becomes a three-pane editor.

screens.name: settings-advanced
screens.note: Absorbs DebugPage + JsonEditor. Config document + danger zone.

screens.name: settings-advanced-health
screens.note: The Advanced screen's Health tab (GET /health, at the root so uptime checks need no token). The mock had the tab and nothing behind it. `skip` is a first-class result, not a failure.

screens.name: nav-accordion
screens.note: Proposal A for the two-vertical-menus problem: the active section expands in the sidebar and Settings loses its 13rem rail; Routing and Activity keep their tab strips. Drawn on Settings -> Server so A and B can be compared on the same screen. Mock-only until one proposal is picked.

screens.name: nav-drilldown
screens.note: Proposal B: the sidebar is replaced by the section's own items, with one row back up. Same screen as A. The trade to judge is that the other four sections leave the screen.

screens.name: nav-tree
screens.note: Proposal C: A applied everywhere, so the tab strips move into the sidebar too. Drawn on Activity -> Requests because that is the only place C differs from A; on a Settings screen the two are the same picture.

screens.name: nav-cloudflare
screens.note: Proposal D: C plus the two things that carry Cloudflare's own deep sidebar - a search field above the tree, and several groups open at once instead of only the current one. Sidebar 16rem. Drawn on Settings -> Server so it lines up with A and B.

screens.name: nav-collapsed
screens.note: Proposal E: what the FOLDED sidebar does with the second level. D won and the sidebar became the only navigation; folding it then dropped Activity's four views and Settings' six sections, which below 1024px (where it folds itself) left them reachable only through the command palette. The rail keeps its icons and the children arrive as a flyout. Mock-only: the collapsed state is a state of every screen, not a route the diff harness can visit.

screens.name: setup
screens.note: Absorbs SetupDialog. First-run explanation before the first question.

screens.name: system-states
screens.note: OAuth ok/error, 404, API-unreachable. Four routes shown together for tone comparison.
